challenge.better_approach: Fixing component_home in cairn/tools/chain/grammar.py would cover every leg, but it reaches a second component; the orchestrator asked for the write, and floor_packet is the one place a chart ref is authored.

answers.falsifier: Done: a floor fed backslash component homes and relpaths stores forward-slash refs, and orient's every_ref_exists accepts them on Linux. Wrong: the backslash enters somewhere other than the floor.
answers.from_idea: none, because the orchestrator measured it on ticket a9709b744bf5 (CairnCommons/tickets/): orient on Linux refused refs the floor cannot verify exist: cairn\devices\cairn, cairn\devices\codemother
answers.how: floor_packet posixes the refs it derives from component_home and _repo_relative (both os.path.relpath, backslash on Windows) at the write; absolute out-of-repo refs stay as written.
answers.traces_to: Law 8 (a proof and a packet read the same on every box); outline 5.5.3.8 (boxes reach one another, so a ref must mean the same on each).
answers.what: Every repo-relative ref the orient floor writes into a chart packet is spelled with forward slashes, whichever box drafted it.
